response.description: A terrestrial ecosystem which is inundated or saturated by surface or ground water at a frequency and duration sufficient to support, and that under normal circumstances does support, a prevalence of vegetation typically adapted for life in saturated soil conditions.
response.label: wetland ecosystem

response.description: An vegetated area which overlaps a wetland ecosystem.
response.label: wetland area

response.description: A wetland ecosystem which overlaps both terrestrial and marine ecosystems.
response.label: coastal wetland ecosystem

response.description: A wetland ecosystem in which soil is saturated with saline water.
response.label: saline wetland

response.description: A wetland which is inundated with water that contains low concentrations of salts.
response.label: freshwater wetland ecosystem

response.description: A wetland ecosystem which is sometimes inundated or saturated by surface or ground water sufficient to support, and that under normal circumstances do support, a prevalence of vegetation typically adapted for life in saturated soil conditions.
response.label: intermittent wetland

response.description: A freshwater littoral zone is a littoral zone which extends offshore from the shore of a freshwater body of water to the limit of occupancy of rooted plants.
response.label: freshwater littoral zone

response.description: According to the NLCD 2011, at least 20% of these areas are covered by forest or shrubland vegetation.  Such thresholds - which are themselves fuzzy - are not strictly asserted in this definition.
response.label: area of woody wetland

response.description: According to the NLCD 2011, at least 80% of these areas are covered by herbaceous vegetation.  Such thresholds - which are themselves fuzzy - are not strictly asserted in this definition.
response.label: area of emergent herbaceous wetland

response.description: A wetland ecosystem which includes communities of grasses, rushes, reeds, typhas, sedges, and other herbaceous plants (possibly with low-growing woody plants).
response.label: marsh

response.description: A wetland ecosystem which accumulates acidic peat, a deposit of dead plant material.
response.label: peatland

response.description: A wetland that forms when mud is deposited by the tides, rivers, sea or oceans.
response.label: mudflat

response.description: A wetland ecosystem in which land mass is permanently inundated by shallow bodies of water, generally with a substantial number of hummocks, or dry-land protrusions.
response.label: swamp ecosystem

response.description: A wet meadow is a type of wetland with soils that are saturated with water for part or all of the growing season.
response.label: wet meadow ecosystem

response.description: It would be more correct to say that this has_quality salty or has_part ((soil and water) and has_increased_levels_of salt.
response.label: saline marsh

response.description: An upland moor or sandy area dominated by low shrubby vegetation including heather.
response.label: heath

response.description: An artificial working of peatland to remove the peat.
response.label: peat cut

response.description: Rain-fed, potentially deep peatlands occurring principally in lowland areas across much of Northern Europe, as well as in the former USSR, North America and parts of the southern hemisphere.
response.label: raised mire

response.description: Flat or concave peatlands with a string-like pattern of hummocks (hence the name), found principally in northern Scandinavia but occurring in the western parts of the former USSR and in North America. A few examples exist in northern Britain.
response.label: string mire

response.description: A freshwater peat land with chemically basic (which roughly means alkaline) ground water.
response.label: fen
